result: 6 coordinator guard tests passed with FUSE runtime
observations: A hung synthetic coordinator was killed by its transient systemd scope deadline and did not write a delayed marker.
After a synthetic coordinator was killed while its 32 MiB ext4-in-FUSE image was mounted, the guard unmounted the recorded fuse.ext4 mount and removed its own backing image.
After SIGKILL of the guard itself, recovery blocked during the watchdog interval; after that interval it unmounted and removed the registered synthetic image.
A forged registration pointing outside the guard root was rejected without modifying the outside file.
The guarded coordinator and one nested executor scope reported memory.max values of 2 GiB and 14 GiB, respectively, and the same four-CPU affinity in a synthetic probe.
A BOOTTIME watcher terminated a registered nested scope at the synthetic session deadline; the same watcher checks after a host resumes, but suspension was not simulated.
limitations: The trusted coordinator uses taskset without no_new_privs to permit the setuid fusermount helper. Candidate sandbox scopes retain their affinity seccomp filter and no_new_privs.

Crash recovery waits until the requested watchdog deadline plus ten seconds when completion was not recorded. This is not a hard real-time proof; system scheduling and startup can overshoot. Unexpected or unregistered resources are preserved for reconciliation.

Only the recorded quota mount and backing image are automatically recovered. Session state files, including ephemeral TLS material, remain inside the private guard root for controlled review and cleanup.

The FUSE test used a 32 MiB synthetic image. The guard checks that a registered backing image does not exceed 100 GiB; this test did not fill a 100 GiB image or establish a full network transfer ceiling. No candidate case was run.
The 2 GiB plus 14 GiB partition assumes at most one candidate scope and trusted coordinator affinity; other host services are outside the accounting.

The BOOTTIME watcher cannot act while suspended and its post-resume scheduling delay was not measured. If the guard itself is killed, independent per-scope systemd timers remain, and recovery stops recorded scopes before unmounting.
